about.title: About the Foundation
about.subtitle: Born from compassion, guided by medical stewardship, and committed to universal dignity.
about.missionDesc: To alleviate human suffering through accessible free healthcare, defend universal human rights, protect the natural environment, and care for all living beings with selfless integrity.
about.visionDesc: An equitable society where no individual is deprived of medical care due to poverty, where human rights are upheld with justice, and where compassion extends across all communities and wildlife.
about.value1: Humanity First: Every human life holds sacred dignity.
about.value2: Verified Integrity: Zero invented claims; complete transparency in all records.
about.value3: Medical Stewardship: Clinical decisions guided by qualified healthcare professionals.
about.value4: Universal Compassion: Unconditional care regardless of race, faith, or background.
about.legalText: The Zulaid Chaudhary Foundation is currently in the formal process of registration with regulatory bodies ('Registration in progress'). All operations adhere to applicable national and international non-profit legal standards.

founder.title: Founder Profile: Zulaid Chaudhary
founder.subtitle: Leading with humble action, medical family ties, and an uncompromising dedication to the vulnerable.
founder.bio1: Zulaid Chaudhary established the foundation with a clear conviction: that humanitarian work is measured by tangible lives changed rather than bureaucratic declarations. Coming from a respected family of medical professionals—including doctors practicing in the United States and Lahore—he observed early on the catastrophic impact of healthcare inequality on working-class families.
founder.bio2: Prior to formal organizational structuring, the founder has already arranged free, specialized surgical and clinical treatment for approximately 25 to 30 patients facing severe health conditions. Recognizing that individualized assistance must be institutionalized, he initiated the construction of a dedicated charity hospital.
founder.bio3: Under his guidance, the foundation’s vision extends beyond emergency aid to systemic advocacy: defending human rights, promoting peaceful international solidarity, preserving the environment, and protecting animal welfare.
founder.fact1: Facilitated free medical treatment for approximately 25–30 patients to date.
founder.fact2: Charity hospital facility currently under active construction.
founder.fact3: Clinical network supported by family physicians in Pakistan and the United States.

medical.title: Free Medical Assistance Program
medical.subtitle: Ensuring life-saving surgeries and specialized clinical care are accessible without financial barriers.
medical.overview: Through an established network of partner doctors and healthcare specialists, the foundation facilitates comprehensive medical treatment for underprivileged patients. The founder has already successfully arranged free treatment for approximately 25-30 patients.
medical.step1Desc: Submission of medical history, diagnostic reports, and hospital cost estimates for review.
medical.step2Desc: Consultation with advisory physicians to verify medical urgency and treatment pathway.
medical.step3Desc: Direct disbursement to healthcare facilities or pharmacy partners—never untracked cash.
medical.step4Desc: Monitoring patient recovery with strict confidentiality and informed consent protocols.

hospital.title: Hospital Construction Project
hospital.subtitle: Building a permanent sanctuary of healing and compassionate care.
hospital.overview: A dedicated charity hospital is under construction to serve as a sustainable healthcare anchor for needy communities. Once completed, the facility will provide emergency, surgical, outpatient, and diagnostic services free of financial strain for deserving families.
hospital.disclaimer: Detailed specifications regarding city location, bed capacity, and department launch schedules will be officially updated as verified milestones are reached.

humanRights.justiceDesc: Advocating for the rights of marginalized laborers, prisoners of poverty, and vulnerable minorities through verified legal and social documentation.
